answer: Bind each identity to a mutual-insurance bridge pool of twelve agents: each locks 100 POA for 60 days, and if one member is caught faking, the whole pool loses 20% of its stake, so pool-mates police each other instead of looking away. A second identity must join a new pool and pay a 200 POA entry fee, a third 400 POA, so entry cost doubles per fake. Even in a gale of new sign-ups, shared risk keeps the nadir of trust high: auditors verify pool locks, membership and slashing events on-ledger before any reward releases.
